html:
Epaminondas was a Theban general and statesman who broke the power of Sparta and made Thebes, for a short time, the leading city of Greece. He was born between 419 and 411 BCE and was killed in battle in 362 BCE.

He came from a poor but noble family and was taught by a Pythagorean philosopher. With his friend Pelopidas he helped lead Thebes after it threw out a Spartan garrison in 379 BCE.

  • At the Battle of Leuctra in 371 BCE he made his left wing fifty ranks deep and smashed the Spartan right, where their best men stood. It was the first time a Spartan army of this size had been beaten in open battle.
  • He then invaded the Peloponnese, freed Messenia from Spartan rule and built the walled city of Messene for its people.
  • He was killed at the Battle of Mantinea in 362 BCE, in the moment of another victory. With him gone, Theban power faded.

As a boy hostage in Thebes, the young Philip of Macedon saw his army at close hand, and took the lessons home.
